sources.entry: TunnelFlow - Modern SSH tunnel and port forwarding manager supporting local, remote, and dynamic SOCKS5 forwards. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/XRSec/TunnelFlow) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: TunnelFlow is a cross-platform desktop app (built with Tauri) for managing SSH tunnels and port forwards, including local, remote, and dynamic SOCKS5 forwarding.
summary.what_it_does: TunnelFlow provides a graphical manager for SSH tunnels, supporting Local forward (-L), Remote forward (-R), and Dynamic SOCKS5 (-D) configurations. Tunnels can be reordered by drag and drop with group hierarchy support. It has a bilingual interface (English and Simplified Chinese) with a native macOS application menu. A system tray menu and a compact 370x660 Mini Mode are included. It shows real-time traffic metrics and handles auto-reconnection with heartbeat checks and configurable retry settings. The README also describes a Web preview mode for development.
use_cases: manage multiple SSH tunnels from a GUI
set up local port forwarding to reach a remote service
expose a local port through a remote SSH server
run a SOCKS5 proxy over SSH
keep SSH tunnels alive with auto-reconnect
notable: Supports local (-L), remote (-R), and dynamic SOCKS5 (-D) SSH forwards in one tool
Heartbeat checks, visual retry configuration, and process lifecycle management for reconnection
Compact 370x660 Mini Mode and native system tray integration
Bilingual English and Simplified Chinese UI with instant toggle
caveats: README does not state platform-specific limitations beyond listing macOS, Windows, and Linux as targets
README does not name a license
keywords: gui alternative to ssh command line
